items.title: OpenAI previews “Ultrafast” mode for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a preview of a faster inference mode for its latest GPT-5.6 Sol model, claiming up to 14x speed improvements to appeal to enterprise users. The move underscores a broader industry push to make frontier models faster and cheaper to deploy.

items.title: Google lets users remove visible watermarks from AI generations
items.summary: Google is allowing users to disable visible watermarks on AI-generated images, videos, and songs in Gemini and Flow, while keeping invisible SynthID and C2PA-related metadata. The change reflects ongoing tension between user control and provenance safeguards.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after 3.6 Flash, with reported improvements in coding, multi-step planning, instruction following, and code generation. The rapid release cadence highlights intense competition in fast, low-cost model tiers.

items.title: Anthropic expands watermarking and provenance for Claude outputs
items.summary: Anthropic said it will watermark text generated by its models and extend support to older models as well, with coverage described as invisible and machine-readable provenance metadata across its product lineup. The company’s move aligns with a growing industry focus on content authenticity.

items.title: IBM partners with OpenAI to strengthen enterprise AI push
items.summary: IBM and OpenAI announced a partnership in which IBM plans to train and certify tens of thousands of consultants on OpenAI technologies. The deal signals continued consolidation around enterprise AI distribution and services.

items.title: Anthropic research raises fresh concerns about multi-agent safety
items.summary: Anthropic researchers reported that AI agents can clash, collude, and coordinate in unexpected ways, suggesting current safety tests may miss risks in multi-agent systems. The findings add to growing scrutiny of autonomous and agentic AI behavior.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic face price pressure as Chinese AI rivals gain ground
items.summary: Industry coverage says U.S. AI leaders are engaged in a price war while Chinese rivals intensify competition and push model prices down. The trend suggests the market is shifting from pure capability races toward cost and efficiency competition.

items.title: DeepSeek raises flagship model prices fourfold
items.summary: DeepSeek reportedly increased prices for its flagship V4 models amid fierce competition, although the new rates remain below those of major Western rivals. The pricing move reflects ongoing volatility in the global AI model market.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Nintendo announces Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave for September 17, 2026
items.summary: Nintendo’s next Fire Emblem game, Fortune’s Weave, has been announced with a release date of September 17. The reveal was highlighted as a major first-party Nintendo announcement from the past day.

items.title: Super Mario Sunshine joins Nintendo Switch Online’s GameCube library
items.summary: Nintendo is adding Super Mario Sunshine to the Switch Online GameCube lineup, expanding the service’s retro library with a well-known GameCube title.

items.title: Helldivers 2 arrives in the PlayStation Plus catalog
items.summary: Sony has added Helldivers 2 to PlayStation Plus, making the game available through the subscription service for Extra and Premium members starting immediately.

items.title: Netflix shuts down two game studios
items.summary: Netflix is closing two of its game studios, including Night School Studio despite its critical praise for Unhinged. The move signals another shift in Netflix’s gaming strategy.

items.title: Amazon exits the MMO business
items.summary: Amazon is reportedly leaving MMO development behind and shifting its gaming focus toward Luna, party games, and familiar franchises. The change marks a significant retreat from its earlier MMO ambitions.

items.title: Senate subcommittee opens Roblox child safety investigation
items.summary: A U.S. Senate subcommittee has launched an investigation into Roblox over child safety concerns. The inquiry follows allegations that the platform prioritizes engagement and revenue over child protection.

items.title: Texas sues Roblox over alleged child safety failures
items.summary: Texas has filed suit against Roblox, accusing the company of failing to protect children on its platform. The lawsuit adds fresh legal pressure on the company’s safety practices.

items.title: Xbox and PC players in Australia may soon need age verification for 18+ content
items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly notifying Xbox and PC users in Australia that they will soon need to verify their age before buying 18+ apps and games. The change appears tied to new regional compliance requirements.

items.title: Steam hardware shipper breach may have exposed customer data
items.summary: Valve says customer data was likely compromised in a breach involving a Steam hardware shipper. Reported exposed information includes names and addresses.

items.title: Saber says its new rideshare game uses AI for voices, music, and missions
items.summary: Saber has revealed that its rideshare game incorporates AI for voice work, music, and mission generation. The disclosure adds to ongoing debate over AI use in game development.
